title: Sell Mineral Rights in Castleberry, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Castleberry, AL | Conecuh County
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Castleberry, AL? Get a hedged, activity-based cash offer for Conecuh County land near the McKenzie Field trend.
heroLead: Castleberry grew up as a rail and timber town in northern Conecuh County, and the mineral rights under its surrounding farmland followed the same leasing waves that touched most of south Alabama during the mid-century oil years.
intro: A number of the families we work with around Castleberry trace their land back several generations, often to a homestead that was later subdivided among children and grandchildren without a formal survey ever separating each person's share. When a mineral interest sits underneath land like that, confirming who owns what percentage can take more work than the sale itself.
We buy interests at any stage of that process, whether ownership is already cleanly documented or still needs to be traced through an old probate file at the courthouse.

sections.heading: Geology near Castleberry
paragraphs: Castleberry sits within reach of the Smackover-Norphlet trend that runs through this part of Conecuh County toward the McKenzie Field and other small prospects nearby. Activity here has always been thinner and more cyclical than in Mobile or Escambia County, so we lean on recent permit filings rather than assuming steady development.

sections.heading: Undivided family tracts
paragraphs: It's common around Castleberry for a mineral interest to sit inside a larger family tract that was never formally partitioned, meaning several relatives each hold an undivided percentage of the whole rather than a specific mapped acreage. We buy interests in that condition and help confirm each owner's actual share as part of the process.

sections.heading: What we need to move forward
paragraphs: A deed, a will, or even just a name and approximate legal description is usually enough to start tracing ownership through Conecuh County's records in Evergreen. From there we check current activity in the surrounding trend and put together a range specific to your tract.

faqs.question: Our family land near Castleberry was never surveyed into individual shares. Can you still buy our interest?
faqs.answer: Yes. We regularly work with undivided interests and help confirm each family member's percentage through county probate and deed records before making an offer.

faqs.question: Is there any current drilling near Castleberry?
faqs.answer: Activity in this part of Conecuh County has historically been thin and cyclical. We check recent permit filings for the specific area before discussing a range.

faqs.question: What if we're not sure exactly where our property lines are?
faqs.answer: We can work from whatever legal description exists in your deed or the courthouse record and help clarify boundaries as part of confirming ownership.

faqs.question: Does selling mean giving up the surface land too?
faqs.answer: No. A mineral sale covers only the oil, gas, and mineral estate, not the surface, unless a deed specifically states otherwise.
